component.subject: Adoration
component.author: Theodulf of Orléans
component.source: Theodulf of Orléans, "Gloria, laus et honor" (Versus facti ut a pueris in die palmarum cantarentur), lines 1–12, in Dümmler, Poetae Latini Aevi Carolini, vol. 1 (1881), carmen 69, p. 558. Unrhymed translation by Russell Allen, CC0; the first couplet, the refrain, is repeated at the end. J. M. Neale's metrical version is "All glory, laud and honour".

original.p: Gloria, laus et honor tibi sit, rex Christe redemptor, cui puerile decus prompsit osanna pium.
Israhel es tu rex, Davidis et inclita proles, nomine qui in domini, rex benedicte, venis.
Coetus in excelsis te laudat caelicus omnis, et mortalis homo et cuncta creata simul.
Plebs Hebraea tibi cum palmis obvia venit: cum prece, voto, hymnis adsumus ecce tibi.
Hi tibi passuro solvebant munia laudis, nos tibi regnanti pangimus ecce melos.
Hi placuere tibi: placeat devotio nostra, rex pie, rex clemens, cui bona cuncta placent.

p.line: Glory, praise and honour to you, Christ, Redeemer, King.
To you the lips of children made sweet hosannas ring!
You are Israel's King, David's noble Son.
Blessed King, you come in the name of the Lord.
All heaven praises you on high,
mortal humanity and all creation join them.
The Hebrews came before you bearing palms.
We come before you now with prayers, with vows, with hymns.
They gave their praise as you went toward your suffering.
We sing to you now that you reign.
Their devotion pleased you — may ours please you too,
good King, gentle King, you who delight in all that is good.
Glory, praise and honour to you, Christ, Redeemer, King.
To you the lips of children made sweet hosannas ring!
